ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r16.claim: The lam in لتستووا is most naturally a purpose lam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r16.anchor: واللام في لتستووا: الظاهر أنها لام كي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r17.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r17.claim: Al-Hawfi allows a consequential lam for those who recognize that category.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r17.anchor: وقال الحوفي: ومن أثبت لام الصيرورة جاز له أن يقول به هنا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r18.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r18.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls it an imperative lam; Abu Hayyan considers this far-fetched because the imperative normally does not use the مخاطب ta form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r18.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لام الأمر، وفيه بعد من حيث استعمال أمر المخاطب بتاء الخطاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r19.claim: Imperatives addressed with ta, such as لتضرب, are rare and poor usage, scarcely preserved outside a noncanonical reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r19.anchor: بل نص النحويون على أنها لغة رديئة قليلة، إذ لا تكاد تحفظ إلا قراءة شاذة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r20.claim: A Prophetic wording with a ta-form imperative is possibly transmitted by meaning rather than verbatim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r20.anchor: وما آثر المحدثون من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام: لتأخذوا مصافاكم، مع احتمال أن الراوي روى بالمعنى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r21.claim: The anomalous example cited for the rare ta-form imperative is فبذلك فلتفرحوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r1.claim: A poem with the imperative لتقم is cited as evidence for an imperative lam addressed with ta.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r1.anchor: لتقم أنت يا ابن خير قريش ... فتقضي حوائج المسلمينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls the imperative lam a good Arabic usage, contrary to the grammarians' judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r2.anchor: وزعم الزجاج أنها لغة جيدة، وذلك خلاف ما زعم النحويون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says the pronoun in ظهوره refers to ما, meaning the backs of what people ride; plural follows the sense and singular would follow the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r3.anchor: والضمير في ظهوره عائد على ما، كأنه قال: على ظهور ما تركبون، قاله أبو عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r4.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r4.claim: Al-Farra gives a similar explanation of the plural reference to the backs of what is ridden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء نحوا منه، قال: أضاف الظهور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r5.claim: Remembering the Lord's favor means recalling it inwardly with gratitude; the following command to say سبحان الله specifies verbal praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r5.anchor: ثم تذكروا، أي في قلوبكم، نعمة ربكم، معترفين بها مستعظمين لها. لا يريد الذكر باللسان بل بالقلب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r6.claim: A prophetic report says that when mounting, the Prophet said basmala, then praise and the Quranic riding supplication, followed by three takbirs and three tahlils.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r6.anchor: في الحديث: «أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب قال: بسم الله، فإذا استوى على الدابة قال: الحمد لله على كل حال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r7.claim: The same report gives a basmala and Quranic supplication when boarding a ship, and a prayer for a blessed landing when disembarking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r7.anchor: وقالوا: إذا ركب في السفينة قال: بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إلى رحيم، ويقال عند النزول منها: اللهم أنزلنا منزلا مباركا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r8.claim: مقرنين describes one strong enough to control something; أقرنه can mean that he was able to handle it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r8.anchor: والقرن: الغالب الضابط المطيق للشيء، يقال: أقرن الشيء، إذا أطاقه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r9.speaker: ابن هرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r9.claim: Ibn Hurma's verse illustrates the difficulty of bearing something one is not strong enough to control.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r9.anchor:
قال ابن هرمة:
وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما ... يطاق احتمال الصدياد عدو الهجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r10.claim: A second derivation explains أقرنه as finding it to be one's companion, since a difficult mount is no companion for the weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r10.anchor: وحقيقة أقرنه: وجده، قرينته وما يقرن به: لأن الصعب لا يكون قرينة للضعف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r11.claim: القرن can also mean the rope by which two things are coupled.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r12.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r12.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses مقرن as able to control someone; the verse says humans lack power to control the mount or ship, which God subjected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: فلان مقرن لفلان، أي ضابط له، والمعنى: أنه ليس لنا من القوة ما نضبط به الدابة والفلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r13.speaker: قطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r13.claim: Qutrub cites Amr ibn Maad Yakrib's verse as evidence for مقرنين.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r13.anchor:
وأنشد قطرب لعمرو بن معد يكرب:
لقد علم القبائل ما عقيل ... لنا في النائبات بمقرنينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r14.claim: A variant reading is لمقترنين, the active participle of اقترن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p361/r14.anchor: وقرىء: لمقترنين، اسم فاعل من اقترن.

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

ABUDAWUD:2599/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:2599/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:2599/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar taught that the Prophet said takbir three times on setting out, recited 43:13–14, and prayed for piety, ease, and protection; on return he added repentance and praise. On climbs the Prophet’s troops said takbir, and downhill they said tasbih.
ABUDAWUD:2599/r1.anchor: أَنَّ ابْنَ عُمَرَ عَلَّمَهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا اسْتَوَى عَلَى بَعِيرِهِ

NAHHAS:v4p100/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p100/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p100/r1.claim: Al-Farra explains the masculine singular pronoun as reflecting the generic sense of the noun, as in kathura al-dirham.
NAHHAS:v4p100/r1.anchor: قال الفراء ولم يقل ظهورها لأنه بمعنى كثر الدرهم أي هو بمعنى الجنس

NAHHAS:v4p100/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p100/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p100/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers that the pronoun refer to the masculine singular form of mā, which also explains the masculine forms ʿalayhi and hādhā.
NAHHAS:v4p100/r2.anchor: وأولى من هذا أن يكون يعود على لفظ ما لأن لفظها مذكر موحد

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r1.claim: The apparent reading makes لام purpose, though it may express result; either way it attaches to جعل.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون هذه لام العلة وهو الظاهر، وأن تكون للصيرورة، فتعلق في كليهما ب " جعل ".

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows a command lām, but al-Samīn finds it far-fetched because it rarely precedes a second-person imperative.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r2.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن تكون للأمر، وفيه بعد لقلة دخولها على أمر المخاطب.

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r3.claim: The rare command-lām pattern appears in فلتفرحوا, a hadith phrase, and poetry; grammarians call it rare except for al-Zajjājī.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r3.anchor: قرئ شاذا " فلتفرحوا " وفي الحديث: " لتأخذوا مصافكم " وقال:

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r4.claim: The pronoun returns to ما تركبون: ظهوره is plural by meaning, while the pronoun is singular by wording.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r4.anchor: الضمير يعود على لفظ " ما تركبون " ، فجمع الظهور باعتبار معناها، وأفرد الضمير باعتبار لفظها.

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r5.claim: له is governed by مقرنين and is fronted to preserve the verse endings.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r5.anchor: " له " متعلق ب " مقرنين " قدم للفواصل.

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r6.claim: مقرنين means able to master or control a thing, from أقرنه, “he made him able”; its underlying sense is finding an equal.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r6.anchor: والمقرن: المطيق للشيء الضابط له، من أقرنه أي: أطاقه. والقرن الحبل.

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r7.claim: Ibn Hurma uses أقرنت to attest ability to bear or control.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r7.anchor: وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما يطاق احتمال الصد يا دعد والهجر

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r8.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maʿd Yakrib’s بمقرنينا witnesses ability to meet an event.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r8.anchor: لقد علم القبائل ما عقيل لنا في النائبات بمقرنينا

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r9.claim: An anonymous verse uses قرن for a tether: a young camel bound there cannot match mature strong camels.
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r9.anchor: وابن اللبون إذا ما لز في قرن لم يستطع صولة البزل القناعيس

SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r10.speaker: قارئ شاذ
SAMIN-DURR:43:13/r10.claim: A noncanonical reading has مقترنين, with an added tāʾ before rāʾ.

ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r4.claim: On mounting, people should praise and exalt God: the ship’s rider says the formula “In God’s name is its course and anchorage,” and the rider of an animal recites the verse’s praise.
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r4.anchor: أي تحمدون الله وتعظمونه، فيقول القائل إذا ركب السفينة: بسم الله مجراها ومرساها،

ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r5.claim: مقرنين means able or capable; it derives from being a match or equal to something, which the riders could not be to these mounts.
ZAJJAJ:v4p406/r5.anchor: أي مطيقين، واشتقاته من قولك: أنا لفلان مقرن أي مطيق،

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r1.claim: Classical commentators take 'their backs' to refer to the backs of both animals and ships; the singular pronoun refers collectively to all conveyances people use.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r1.anchor: according to all classical commentators, the "backs" of the above- mentioned animals and ships alike

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r2.claim: Asad renders istawa as gaining mastery, a connotation supported by Jawhari, Raghib, Lisan al-'Arab, and Lane.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n11/r2.anchor: the verb istawa (lit., "he established himself") has often the connotation adopted by me: see Jawhari, Raghib and Lisan al-'Arab

IBNHIBBAN:2695/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2695/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNHIBBAN:2695/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet, mounting for travel, said takbīr three times, recited the verse, prayed for piety, accepted deeds, an easy journey and protection for his family, and on return praised God as a repentant traveler.
IBNHIBBAN:2695/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سافر فركب راحلته كبر ثلاثا

IBNHIBBAN:2696/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r1.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r1.claim: Ibn Ḥibbān presents this transmission as evidence against the claim that Ḥammād b. Salama alone transmitted Abu al-Zubayr's report.
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r1.anchor: حدثنا ابن وهب، عن ابن جريج، أن أبا الزبير أخبره

IBNHIBBAN:2696/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet mounted for travel, said takbīr three times and recited the verse; he prayed for piety, ease, protection from hardship and a safe return, then repeated the prayer on return with added praise.
IBNHIBBAN:2696/r2.anchor: أن أبا الزبير أخبره، أن عليا الأسدي أخبره، أن عبد الله بن عمر علمه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.speaker: علي بن ربيعة الأسدي
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.claim: ʿAlī b. Rabīʿa recounts that ʿAlī invoked God while mounting, praised His provision and subjection of transport, recited 43:13–14, said takbīr three times and sought forgiveness; he adds that the Prophet did likewise while he rode behind him.
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r1.anchor: عن علي بن ربيعة الأسدي، قال: ركب علي دابة

IBNHIBBAN:2697/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r2.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r2.claim: Ibn Ḥibbān frames ʿAlī's expanded riding invocation as showing that a person may add other phrases to this supplication.
IBNHIBBAN:2697/r2.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أكرمنا، وحملنا في البر والبحر، ورزقنا من الطيبات

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses being unable to master the mount as lacking power or strength to do so in worship.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما كنا له مقرنين ﴾ قال في العبادة في القوة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r2.claim: Ali's mounting invocation begins with God's name, praises Him after settling, recites the verse, praises and magnifies God three times each, then asks forgiveness.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r2.anchor: سمع عليا حين ركب فلما وضع رجله في الركاب قال بسم الله فلما استوى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r3.claim: The Prophet says he marvels at a servant asking forgiveness while knowing that only God forgives sins.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r3.anchor: فقلنا ما يضحك يا نبي الله قال العبد أو قال عجبت للعبد إذا قال لا إله إلا أنت ظلمت نفسي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r4.speaker: طاوس عن أبيه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r4.claim: Ṭāwūs says that when riding, his father invoked God's name, acknowledged the mount as God's bounty, praised God, and recited the verse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#4/r4.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه قال كان إذا ركب قال بسم الله ثم يقول اللهم هذا من منك وفضلك علينا

MUSLIM:3275/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:3275/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
MUSLIM:3275/r1.claim: Ibn Umar taught that the Prophet said the verse and a travel supplication after mounting and saying takbir three times; on returning he repeated it and added that they were returning repentant, worshipping, and praising their Lord.
MUSLIM:3275/r1.anchor: أن ابن عمر علمهم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا استوى على بعيره خارجا إلى سفر كبر ثلاثا ثم قال

MUSNAD-AHMAD:753/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:753/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:753/r1.claim: Ali reports the mount invocation he used and says he saw the Prophet do likewise; the Prophet added that God marvels when a servant asks forgiveness knowing only God forgives.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:753/r1.anchor: قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل مثل ما فعلت، ثم ضحك

MUSNAD-AHMAD:930/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:930/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:930/r1.claim: Ali's riding invocation includes praise, takbīr, and a plea for forgiveness; the Prophet did the same and said God marvels that the servant knows none forgives except Him.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:930/r1.anchor: قال: رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل مثل ما فعلت، وقال: مثل ما قلت، ثم ضحك

MUSNAD-AHMAD:1056/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1056/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1056/r1.claim: Ali reports reciting praise, takbīr, tasbīḥ, and the mount invocation before seeking forgiveness; the Prophet attributed God's amazement to the servant knowing only God forgives.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1056/r1.anchor: كنت ردفا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ففعل كالذي رأيتني فعلت، ثم ضحك

MUSNAD-AHMAD:6311/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6311/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6311/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet recited this invocation when mounting, then prayed for righteousness and piety in travel and praised God on returning home.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6311/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا ركب راحلته كبر ثلاثا

MUSNAD-AHMAD:6374/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6374/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6374/r1.claim: Ibn Umar taught this travel formula: the Prophet recited the verse upon mounting, prayed for piety and ease, sought refuge from travel's hardships, and added a return prayer.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6374/r1.anchor: أن ابن عمر علمه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكان إذا استوى على بعيره خارجا إلى سفر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r1.claim: The wording uses ‘settle’ for all conveyances though it particularly suits mounts; the singular pronoun follows ‘what you ride’ grammatically, while plural ‘backs’ follows its meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r1.anchor: حيث عبر عن القرار على الجميع بالاستواء المخصوص بالدواب والضمير لما تركبون

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r2.claim: Alusi takes the lām as purposive; al-Hawfi allows a consequential lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r2.anchor: أن لام ( لتستووا ) لام كي وقال الحوفي : من أثبت لام للصيرورة جاز له أن يقول به هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls it an imperative lām, which Alusi regards as unlikely because the second-person tāʾ form is rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : هي لام الأمر وفيه بعد من حيث استعماله أمر المخاطب بتاء الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj considers the second-person imperative a good usage; Abu Hayyan prefers the purposive lām and reports it as the majority grammarians’ view.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : إنها لغة جيدة وأبو حيان على الأول وحكاه عن جمهور النحويين

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r5.claim: Examples cited for the rare imperative include an irregular reading, poetry, and a Prophetic phrase that hadith scholars may have transmitted by meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r5.anchor: لا تكاد تحتفظ إلا في قراءة شاذة نحو ( فبذلك فلتفرحوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r6.claim: Remember the blessing inwardly, acknowledging and esteeming it, then praise God aloud; this is gratitude, with inward acknowledgment part of proper remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r6.anchor: أي تذكروها بقلوبكم معترفين بها مستعظمين لها ثم تحمدوا عليها بألسنتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says remembrance entails heart awareness while the intended act is verbal praise, with both together its fullest form; Alusi calls this sound too.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r7.anchor: الزمخشري أن الذكر يتضمن شعور القلب والمراد على اللسان فنزل على أكمل أحواله

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r8.claim: Those who allow a shared word to bear both meanings understand remembrance as inward and verbal.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r8.anchor: ومن جوز استعمال المشترك في معنييه جوز هنا أن يراد بالذكر الذكر القلبي والذكر اللساني

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r9.claim: The utterance declares God exalted for making the conveyance tame; ‘this’ depicts the situation to heighten wonder, not belittle it, and its declarative wording implies a request to say it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r9.anchor: أي وتقولواسبحان الذي ذلله وجعله منقادا لنا متعجبين من ذلك وليس الإشارة للتحقير

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r10.speaker: أبو مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r10.claim: Abu Majliz reports that Husayn ibn Ali corrected a rider by first praising God for Islam, Muhammad, and belonging to the best community, then reciting the travel formula; this points to Islam as the blessing. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r10.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر عن أبي مجلز قال : رأى الحسين بن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r11.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r11.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports that Shahr ibn Hawshab interpreted the blessing as Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن شهر بن حوشب أنه فسرها بنعمة الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.claim: A report from Ali, graded authentic by al-Tirmidhi, gives the mounting supplication: say ‘in God’s name’ at the stirrup, praise and magnify God three times, recite the verses, then seek forgiveness; Ali says the Prophet did likewise and describes God’s delight at the plea.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r12.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وأبو داود والترمذي وصححه والنسائي وجماعة عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.claim: A report in Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and al-Darimi says the Prophet praised, glorified, and magnified God three times when mounting his camel to travel, then recited these verses. No grading is stated here.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r13.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه مسلم والترمذي وأبو داود والدارمي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r14.claim: A report transmitted by Ahmad and others says every camel has a devil on its hump, so riders should invoke God’s name when mounting.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r14.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه أحمد وغيره عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ما من بعير إلا في ذروته شيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r15.claim: The remembrance and formula apply to ships as well as animals; some say ‘In God’s name is its course and anchorage’ when embarking and pray for a blessed landing when disembarking.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67#3/r15.anchor: وظاهر النظم الجليل أن تذكر النعمة والقول المذكور لا يخصان ركوب الأنعام بل يعم إنها والفلك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r1.claim: ‘We could not master it’ means we lacked strength to control the mount or ship; God alone subdued and controlled it.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r1.anchor: ما يضبط به الدابة والفلك وإنما الله تعالى هو الذيسخر ذلك وضبطه لنا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r2.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r2.claim: Qutrub cites Amr ibn Maʿdikarib’s line as evidence that the root can mean being able or matched in strength.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r2.anchor: وأنشد قطرب لعمرو ابن معدي كرب : لقد علم القبائل ما عقيل لنا في نائبات بمقرنينا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r3.speaker: ابن هرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r3.claim: Ibn Harma’s verse is cited as evidence for being capable of what one is made to bear.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r3.anchor: قال ابن هرمة : وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما يطلق احتمال الصدياد عد والهجر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r4.claim: The underlying image is finding something as one’s peer: a difficult mount cannot be a weak person’s equal, and ‘qarn’ can mean the binding rope.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r4.anchor: وحقيقة أقرنه وجده قرينته وما يقرن به لأن الصعب لا يكون قرينة للضعف

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r5.claim: A line about a young camel restrained by a rope shows it cannot withstand the charge of powerful mature camels, illustrating the root’s binding sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر : وابن اللبون إذا ما لز في قرن لم يستطع صولة البزل القناعيس

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r6.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r6.claim: Ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir report that a traveler boasted he could master his powerful camel after reciting the verse; it bucked him down and broke his neck. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r6.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن سليمان بن يسار أن قوما كانوا في سفر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r7.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ, with either fatḥa or kasra; both forms mean the same as the undoubled reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p69/r7.anchor: وقريء ( مقرنين ) بتشديد الراء مع فتحها وكسرها وهما بمعنى المخفف

TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.speaker: النبي
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet recited this verse and 43:14 when mounting for travel, then prayed for piety, accepted deeds, an easier journey, and protection for companions and family; Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan gharīb from this route.
TIRMIDHI:3447/r1.anchor: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا سَافَرَ فَرَكِبَ رَاحِلَتَهُ كَبَّرَ ثَلاَثًا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.claim: The masculine pronoun in zuhurihi refers back to ma, the relative pronoun meaning what you ride.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.anchor: {لتستووا على ظهوره} ذكر الكناية لأنه ردها إلى "ما".

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.claim: The blessing to remember is God's subjection of the mounts and ships for travel on land and sea.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.anchor: {ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه} بتسخير المراكب في البر والبحر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.claim: Sakhkhara means to subdue or make something tractable for people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.anchor: وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا} ذلل لنا هذا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.claim: Muqrinin means capable of controlling it; another explanation is being its masters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.anchor: {وما كنا له مقرنين} مطيقين، وقيل: ضابطين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.claim: Ali ibn Rabia saw Ali recite the mounted supplication, praise and magnify God, seek forgiveness, and laugh; Ali said the Prophet did likewise and marveled at a servant who knows only God forgives sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207#2/r8.anchor: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 117/ب فعل ما فعلت، وقال مثل ما قلت، ثم ضحك، فقلنا: ما يضحكك يا نبي الله؟ قال: "العبد"

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r9.claim: The plural “backs” follows the meaning of the things people ride.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r9.anchor: أي ظهور ما تركبون وجمعه للمعنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r10.claim: Riders should remember the blessing inwardly, acknowledging and praising God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r10.anchor: تذكروها بقلوبكم معترفين بها حامدين عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r11.claim: مقرنين means able to master it; the root suggests finding its counterpart, since a difficult thing cannot be a weak person's peer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r11.anchor: مطيقين من أقرن الشيء إذا أطاقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r12.claim: A doubled reading is also reported, with the same meaning.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r13.claim: The Prophet said “In God's name” when placing his foot in the stirrup, then praised God once settled on the riding animal.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r13.anchor: وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.claim: The return completes the travel imagery: riding entails movement, whose greatest journey is the return to God; alternatively, travel reminds riders of death and to prepare for meeting God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.anchor: واتصاله بذلك لأن الركوب للتنقل والنقلة العظمى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r6.claim: To settle upright on the backs of the ships or animals, balanced, steady, secure, and at ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r6.anchor: أي تكونوا مع الاعتدال والاستقرار والتمكن والراحة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r7.claim: The plural sense of ما makes ظهره refer to the backs of the various mounts, while عليه returns to the singular grammatical form; masculine wording can also signal the mount’s strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r7.anchor: فالضمير عائد على ما جمع الظهر نظرا للمعنى تكثيرا للنعمة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r8.claim: The delayed ثم marks remembrance as a lofty goal beyond receiving the transport benefit; remembrance begins in the heart and recognizes the Lord’s nurturing kindness.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r8.anchor: ذكر ما ينبغي أن يكون من غايتها على ما هو المتعارف بينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r9.claim: Mounting seems ordinary only through familiarity: the balance and stability are extraordinary, as shown by animals that cannot be ridden and inanimate things at sea that cannot carry people.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r9.anchor: ولما كان الاعتدال عليه أمرا خارفا للعادة بدليل ما لا يركب من الحيوانات في البر والجوامد في البحر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r10.claim: Remembering the blessing should move the heart, tongue, and limbs to gratitude; the verse specifically requires speaking thanks aloud as well as remembering inwardly.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r10.anchor: أي بألسنتكم جمعا بين القلب واللسان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r11.claim: Riding exposes human dependence on the mount to reach a destination and remain safe; God’s ease in helping the helpless shows his transcendence, and his enthronement is unlike creaturely sitting.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r11.anchor: وأن استواءه على عرشه ليس كهذا الاستواء المقارن لهذه النقائص

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r12.claim: God subjected the mount through his complete knowledge and perfect power.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r13.claim: People were not naturally able to match, master, or overpower a mount stronger than they are; أقرن الأمر means to have the capacity and strength for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r13.anchor: أي ما كان في جبلتنا إطاقة أن يكون قرنا له وحده لخروج قوته من بين ما نعالجه ونعانيه عن طاقتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.claim: Ali’s report says that on mounting he said Bismillah, then praised God for subjecting the mount, praised and magnified God three times, and sought pardon; the author cites the Tirmidhi grading hasan sahih.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r5.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه وضع رجله في الركاب وقال : بسم الله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.claim: In Ali’s report, the Prophet did likewise and said God marvels at the servant who asks pardon, knowing that only God forgives sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r6.anchor: وأخبر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل مثله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet rode with him, recited takbir, praise, and glorification three times each, then tahlil once, leaned back, and laughed; he described God’s smiling response to a rider who does likewise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه على دابة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet said the riding glorification and then prayed for righteousness and piety, accepted deeds, an easy journey, and care for his family; the cited collections are Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and al-Tirmidhi.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p12/r8.anchor: وروى أحمد ومسلم وأبو داود والنسائي والترمذي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا ركب راحلته

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports mounting with God's name, praising and magnifying Him, reciting both verses, and asking forgiveness; he had seen the Prophet do likewise.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r1.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه أتى بدابة فلما وضع رجله في الركاب قال: بسم الله فلما استوى على ظهرها

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.claim: The Prophet says God marvels at a servant asking forgiveness, knowing only God forgives sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r2.anchor: فقلت يا رسول الله: مم ضحكت فقال: يعجب الرب من عبده إذا قال: رب اغفر لي

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet magnifying God three times and declaring His unity after settling on the mount, then laughing.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه على دابته فلما استوى عليها (كبر ثلاثا

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r4.speaker: محمد بن حمزة بن عمر الأسلمي
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r4.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ḥamza reports his father quoting the Prophet: a devil is above every camel, so name God when riding and pursue needs.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن حمزة بن عمر الأسلمي عن أبيه رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: فوق ظهر كل بعير شيطان

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a devil on each camel's hump; riders should humble the animals, since God alone carries.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: على ذروة كل بعير شيطان فامتهنوهن بالركوب

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r6.speaker: أبو لاس الخزاعي
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r6.claim: Abū Lās reports the Prophet warning that every camel has a devil and commanding riders to name God and ride humbly.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r6.anchor: عن أبي لاس الخزاعي رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما من بعير إلا في ذروته شيطان

DURR-FULL:v7p368/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r7.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r7.claim: Shahr identifies the bounty recalled when mounted as Islam.
DURR-FULL:v7p368/r7.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب رضي الله عنه في قوله {ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه} قال: نعمة الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.claim: Abū Mujliz says Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī taught a rider first to praise God for Islam, Muḥammad, and making the community best for humanity, then recite these verses.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r1.anchor: عن أبي مجلز رضي الله عنه قال: رأى حسين بن علي رضي الله عنه رجلا يركب دابة فقال {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.claim: Ṭāwūs thanked God for the gift and bounty of the ride and recited both verses when mounting.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r2.anchor: عن طاوس رضي الله عنه أنه كان إذ ركب دابة قال: بسم الله اللهم هذا من منك وفضلك علينا فلك الحمد

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r3.claim: Mujāhid lists camels, horses, mules, and donkeys as the mounts in view.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وما كنا له مقرنين} قال: الإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as meaning people could not master the mounts.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وما كنا له مقرنين}

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r5.claim: Qatāda says people could manage the mounts neither by hand nor strength.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وما كنا له مقرنين} قال: لا في الأيدي ولا في القوة

DURR-FULL:v7p369/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r6.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r6.claim: Sulaymān recounts a traveler boasting he could master his stubborn camel; it threw him and broke his neck.
DURR-FULL:v7p369/r6.anchor: عن سليمان بن يسار رضي الله عنه أن قوما كانوا في سفر فكانوا إذا ركبوا قالوا: {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3281#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3281#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3281#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “we could not master it” as “we were not able.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3281#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : وما كنا له مقرنين قال : مطيقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.claim: The eleven second-person pronouns across these four verses follow the expected address and are not iltifat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.anchor: وضمائر الخطاب الأحد عشر الواقعة في الآيات الأربع من قوله : { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r5.claim: الاستواء means climbing onto; ظهور ordinarily relates to livestock, so the expression generalizes to animal backs and ships' interiors and upper decks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r5.anchor: والاستواء الاعتلاء . والظهور : جمع ظهر ، والظهر من علائق الأنعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r6.claim: The pronoun returns to ما, which denotes ships and livestock; large ships have upper surfaces shielding riders from rain, heat, and cold.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r6.anchor: فضمير { ظهوره } عائد إلى { ما } الموصولة الصادق بالفلك والأنعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r7.claim: ظهور uses the shared sense of animal backs and ship surfaces, and على is used because ships have an upper surface.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r7.anchor: ولذلك فجمع الظهور من جمع المشترك والتعدية بحرفف { على } بنيت على أن للسفينة ظهرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r8.claim: Settling on a mount prepares riders to remember God's blessing while experiencing its benefits, when gratitude is more affecting and less likely to lapse; ذكر here is mental recollection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r8.anchor: وقد جعل قوله : { لتستووا على ظهوره } توطئة وتمهيدا للإشارة إلى ذكر نعمة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r9.claim: This alludes to polytheists enjoying God's gifts yet thanking other gods that did not share in creating livestock; recalling the gift stands for thanking its giver.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p173/r9.anchor: وهذا تعريض بالمشركين إذ تقلبوا في نعم الله وشكروا غيره إذ اتخذوا له شركاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r1.claim: The formula adds inward thanks with public verbal thanks; God teaches it as He teaches praise in al-Fatiha and supplication at al-Baqara's end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r1.anchor: فلقنهم صيغة شكر عناية به كما لقنهم صيغة الحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r2.claim: Verbal thanks begins with tasbih, which explicitly negates defects and implicitly affirms perfections, thus gathering praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r2.anchor: وافتتح هذا الشكر اللساني بالتسبيح لأنه جامع للثناء إذ التسبيح تنزيه الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r3.claim: The relative clause explains why God is praised; هذا points to the animal or ship on which the speaker rides.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r3.anchor: واستحضار الجلالة بطريق الموصولية لما يؤذن به الموصول من علة التسبيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r4.claim: تسخير means making pliant and compliant: animals are trainable and responsive, and ships work through a navigable sea, winds, human ingenuity, sails, and oars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r4.anchor: تسخير الله الدواب هو خلقه إياها قابلة للترويض فاهمة لمراد الراكب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r5.claim: مقرنين means capable or able; أقرن means to be able, as witnessed by Amr ibn Ma'dikarib's verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r5.anchor: قال عمرو بن معديكرب : لقد علم القبائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r6.claim: Humans could not manage the mount by bodily strength alone; this clause is circumstantial to لنا, describing divine subjection as a substitute for our strength.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p174/r6.anchor: أي بمجرد القوة الجسدية ، أي لولا التسخير المذكور ، فجملة { وما كنا له مقرنين }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r5.claim: The lām in litastawū may be an imperative lām or a lām of purpose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله: لتستووا لام الأمر، ويحتمل أن تكون لام كي،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r7.claim: The verse on what to say when boarding a ship is Hud 11:41; this passage concerns animal mounts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r7.anchor: وقد بينت آية ما يقال عند ركوب الفلك، وهو: بسم الله مجراها ومرساها، إن ربي لغفور رحيم [هود: 41]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r8.claim: The boat formula is specific to animal mounts here; on disembarking one asks God for a blessed landing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r8.anchor: وإنما هذه خاصة فيما يركب من الحيوان، ويقال (-) عند النزول منها: اللهم أنزلنا منزلا مباركا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r9.claim: The rider's sunnah is to praise God for Islam, for Muhammad, or for blessing in every circumstance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r9.anchor: والسنة للراكب إذا ركب أن يقول: الحمد لله على نعمة الإسلام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r10.claim: A formula of riding praise, including this verse's wording, is reported from Ali as a saying of the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r10.anchor: وقد روي هذا اللفظ عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: سبحان الذي الآية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r11.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r11.claim: Abu Majliz rode and said the سبحان الله formula without mentioning the blessing; al-Hasan ibn Ali corrected him and taught praise for guidance to Islam first.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r11.anchor: وسمعه الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما فقال: ما هكذا أمرتم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r12.speaker: طاوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r12.claim: Tawus first said that the mount was from God's grace and favor, then recited the verse's formula.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r12.anchor: وكان طاوس إذا ركب قال: اللهم هذا من منك وفضلك، ثم يقول: سبحان الذي الآية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r13.claim: If recalling the blessing is inward, the rider may begin with glorification while recognizing God's blessing in the mount and elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r13.anchor: وإن قدرنا أن ذكر النعمة هو بالقلب والتذكير بدأ الراكب: ب سبحان الذي سخر، وهو يرى نعمة الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r14.claim: Muqrin means one who masters, controls, dominates, or is capable of a thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r14.anchor: والمقرن: الغالب الضابط المستولي على الأمر المطيق له.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r15.speaker: أعرابي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r15.claim: A Bedouin boasted that he could master his camel; it threw him, broke his neck, and killed him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r15.anchor: وروي أن بعض الأعراب ركب جملا فقيل له قل: سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.claim: A report says that if a rider omits this verse, Satan tells him to sing, or, if unable, to indulge fantasies and waste the time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p48/r2.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الإنسان إذا ركب ولم يقل هذه الآية جاءه الشيطان فقال: «تغنه،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r1.claim: The material through this phrase had already been explained at Ya-Sin 42.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r1.anchor: وما بعد هذا قد سبق يس 36 42 إلى قوله تعالى ﴿ لتستووا على ظهوره ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says the pronoun hāʾ in “its backs” refers to mā, the thing people ride.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة هاء التذكير ل ما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r3.claim: The remembered blessing is God's subjection of the vehicle for people on land and sea.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r3.anchor: إذ سخر لكم ذلك المركب في البر والبحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret muqrinin as able or capable.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد أي مطيقين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains muqrinin as able, using an idiom for being one's equal in strength; qarn with open qaf can mean someone of the same age.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة يقال أنا مقرن لك أي مطيق لك ويقال هو من قولهم أنا قرن لفلان إذا كنت مثله في الشدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets muqrinin as having control, citing an idiom for one person being able to control another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة مقرنين أي ضابطين يقال فلان مقرن لفلان أي ضابط له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r8.claim: People are enabled to sit securely and comfortably on the backs of this kind, remember God’s favor for subjecting it, and glorify Him because they could not control it without His subjection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r8.anchor: أي: لتستووا (4) متمكنين مرتفقين {على ظهوره} أي: على ظهور هذا الجنس، {ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم} أي: فيما سخر لكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r9.claim: The phrase means people were not able to master or match the conveyance; without God’s subjection they could not manage it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r9.anchor: مقاومين. ولولا تسخير (5) الله لنا هذا ما قدرنا عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، السدي، وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd gloss muqrinin as people who are capable of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس (6) ، وقتادة، والسدي وابن زيد: {مقرنين} أي: مطيقين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.claim: Ali reports his mounting praise and supplication, then the Prophet's similar practice and teaching that God knows only He forgives sins; Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih, with variant transmission routes noted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p220/r2.anchor: حديث أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet praised God, proclaimed His oneness, reclined and laughed, then said God smiles toward a Muslim rider who does likewise; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's riding and travel supplications, including the return formula; Muslim, Abu Dawud, Nasa'i, and Tirmidhi transmit it through routes from Abu al-Zubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p221/r2.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن عمر، رضي الله عنهما

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r3.claim: People rise upon the backs of what they ride; backs literally fit livestock rather than ships, giving livestock semantic precedence.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r3.anchor: لتستعلوا على ظهور ما تركبونه من الفلك والأنعام والظهور للأنعام حقيقة لا للفلك

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r4.claim: The plural ẓuhūr is used although its possessor is singular in form because its referent is plural in meaning.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r4.anchor: وإيراد لفظ ظهور بصيغة الجمع مع أن ما أضيف مفرد إليه للمعنى ؛ لأن مرجع الضمير جمع في المعنى

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r5.claim: Remembrance is primarily in the heart; this explains choosing remember rather than praise, followed by inward acknowledgment and spoken praise.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r5.anchor: والمراد الذكر بالقلوب ؛ لأنه هو الأصل.

BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r6.claim: A prophetic report says God looks to hearts and intentions rather than outward forms and deeds.
BURSEVI:v8p272#2/r6.anchor: فقد ورد "إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم وأعمالكم بل إلى قلوبكم ونياتكم".

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r1.claim: The riders say the glorification in amazement at the subduing of their mount.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r1.anchor: {وتقولوا} متعجبين من ذلك. {سبحان الذى سخر لنا هاذا} : المركوب

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r2.claim: God made the ship and animal docile and subject to people, enabling travel over land and sea.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r2.anchor: يعني : (باكست آن خداى كه رام ونرم كردانيد وزيردست ساخت براى ما اين كشتى واين حيوانرا

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r3.claim: Muqrinin means able to tame, match, and control the mount; humans lack that strength, and God subdues it by power and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r3.anchor: {وما كنا له مقرنين} ؛ أي : مطيقين بتذليلها يعني : ليس عندنا من القوة والطاقة أن نقرن هذه الدابة والفلك

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r4.claim: Recognizing incapacity to secure a blessing is necessary to know its worth and the benefactor's due.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r4.anchor: وهذا من تمام ذكر نعمته تعالى إذ بدون اعتراف المنعم عليه بالعجز عن تحصيل النعمة لا يعرف قدرها

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r5.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r5.claim: Al-Qamus glosses aqran as being able and strong enough, contrasting it with weakness.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r5.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : أقرن الأمر أطاقه وقوي عليه ، كاستقرن وعن الأمر ضعف ضد

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r6.claim: Kashf al-Asrar explains iqran as controlling someone and matching his strength, or becoming his equal; this clarifies the capacity humans lack against the mount.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r6.anchor: ليس عندنا من القوة والطاقة أن نقرن هذه الدابة والفلك

BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r7.claim: Another etymology derives the word from finding something as one's match: what matches a person is not difficult for him, hence the sense of ability.
BURSEVI:v8p272#3/r7.anchor: وقال غيره : أصله وجده قرينه ؛ لأن الصعب لا يكون قرينا للضعيف

BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r1.claim: A traveler on a famished, motionless she-camel boasted he could master it; it leapt, threw him, and broke his neck.
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r1.anchor: وروي : أن قوما ركبوا في سفر ، وقالوا : {سبحان الذى} ، الآية. وفيهم رجل على ناقة رازمة ، لا تتحرك هزالا

BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r2.speaker: الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r2.claim: When his mount stumbled, Hasan ibn Ali prayed that omens and good belong to God, with no refuge or power except through Him; aboard ship he recited 11:41 and 39:67.
BURSEVI:v8p273#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما : أنه كان إذا عثرت دابته. قال : اللهم لا طير إلا طيرك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r3.claim: Their backs means the backs of the things people ride, both ships and livestock.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r3.anchor: على ظهور ما تركبونه وهو الفلك والأنعام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r4.claim: Remembering the blessing means acknowledging and esteeming it inwardly, then praising God for it aloud.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r4.anchor: أن يذكروها في قلوبهم معترفين بها مستعظمين لها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.claim: The Prophet said In God’s name when putting a foot in the stirrup, then praised God and recited through we shall return after mounting, adding three takbīrs and three declarations of oneness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r6.claim: They said that when boarding a ship one should say In God’s name is its course and anchorage (11:41).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r6.anchor: إذا ركب في السفينة قال : { بسم الله مجراها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r7.speaker: الحسن بن علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī corrected a man who recited the glorification but omitted praise, reminding him to remember God’s blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما أنه رأى رجلا يركب دابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r8.claim: The correction illustrates the early community’s care for fine details of religious etiquette.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r8.anchor: من حسن مراعاتهم لآداب الله ومحافظتهم على دقيقها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r9.claim: Muqrinīn means able to master something; Arabic uses aqrana for having the capacity to do it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r9.anchor: مطيقين . يقال : أقرن الشيء ، إذا أطاقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r10.speaker: ابن هرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r10.claim: Ibn Hurmā’s verse uses aqrant to mean being able to bear the beloved’s rejection and estrangement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r10.anchor: قال ابن هرمة : وأقرنت ما حملتني ولقلما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r11.claim: The underlying sense is to find something a match or companion: a difficult beast cannot be paired with a weak rider.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p243/r12.claim: A variant reads muqarrinīn with the same meaning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r14.claim: The singular ‘backs’ denotes a generic class and therefore carries plural meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r14.anchor: وأضاف الظهور إلى واحد لأن المراد به الجنس فصار الواحد في معنى الجمع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r15.claim: Being settled on it means riding it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r15.anchor: { ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه } أي ركبتم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r16.claim: God subdued the mount by making it compliant as a vehicle.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r17.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses the word as having control over it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r17.anchor: ضابطين , قاله الأخفش . الثاني : مماثلين في الأيد والقوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r18.claim: Qatāda takes it as equal in strength to the mount, from the saying that one is another’s equal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r18.anchor: مماثلين في الأيد والقوة , قاله قتادة من قولهم هو قرن فلان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r19.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Kalbī gloss it as able or capable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r19.anchor: مطيقين , قاله ابن عباس والكلبي , وأنشد قطرب لعمرو بن معدي كرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r20.claim: Al-Māwardī cites Qutrub’s verse by ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib as evidence for ‘capable.’
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r20.anchor: وأنشد قطرب لعمرو بن معدي كرب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r1.claim: One derivation is iqran, used when someone is able.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r1.anchor: أصله مأخوذ من الإقران , يقال أقرن فلان إذا أطاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r2.claim: Another derivation is muqārana: joining things together while traveling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r2.anchor: أصله مأخوذ من المقارنة وهو أن يقرن بعضها ببعض في السير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r3.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r3.claim: Sulaymān b. Yasār tells of travelers reciting the verse; one man boasted he could manage his emaciated, unmoving camel, which threw him and broke his neck.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p218/r3.anchor: وحكى سليمان بن يسار أن قوما كانوا في سفر , فكانوا إذا ركبوا قالوا

MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.claim: Ibrahim reports that ʿAlqama ibn Qays said Bismillah before mounting, praised God once seated, and recited the riding supplication when the animal rose.
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال وضع علقمة بن قيس رجله في الغرز فقال بسم الله فلما قعد على ظهرها قال الحمد لله فلما نهض قال

MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says the animals described as subjected are camels, horses, mules, and donkeys.
MUJAHID:v2p579#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وما كنا له مقرنين ﴾ يعني الإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r5.claim: “So that you may settle” means “so that you may sit”; the backs are male and female camels.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r5.anchor: لتستووا } ، يعني لكي تستووا، { على ظهوره } ، يعني ذكورا وإناثا من الإبل

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r6.claim: Mounted on their backs, riders remember their Lord’s blessing by saying, “Praise be to God.”
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r6.anchor: ثم } قال: لكي { تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه } ، على ظهورها

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r7.claim: The one who subjected the mount made the vehicle docile for riders.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r7.anchor: وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا } ، يعني ذلل لنا هذا المركب

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r8.claim: Muqrinin means capable of mastering or controlling the mount.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r8.anchor: وما كنا له مقرنين } [آية: 13]، يعني مطيقين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.claim: Their backs are the backs of the things they ride: ships and livestock.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.anchor: على ظهور ما تركبونه وهو الفلك والأنعام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.claim: On boarding, remember God's blessing in the heart and utter the glorification with the tongue.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.anchor: ثم تذكروا بقلوبكم ﴿ نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا ﴾ بألسنتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.claim: Sakhkhara here means He made this conveyance submissive and manageable for us.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.claim: Muqrinīn means able to master it; aqranahu means he was able to manage it, literally finding it a peer, since a hard thing is no peer to a weak person.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.anchor: مطيقين يقال أقرن الشيء إذا أطاقه وحقيقة اقرنه وجده قرينته لأن الصعب لا يكون قرينة للضعيف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.claim: The Prophet's travel prayer begins when he puts a foot in the stirrup and continues after mounting through the words of return to God; he then says takbīr three times and tahlīl three times. For a ship, he recited the Qur'anic prayer bismillāhi majrāhā wa mursāhā, inna rabbī la-ghafūrun raḥīm.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r3.anchor: وعن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب قال بسم الله فإذا استوى على الدابة قال الحمد لله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r4.claim: An anecdote tells of a man on a still, emaciated camel who declared himself able to control it; it bucked, he fell, and his neck broke.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p110#3/r4.anchor: وحكى أن قوما ركبوا وقالوا سبحان الذى سخر لنا هذا الآية وفيهم رجل على ناقة لا تتحرك هزالا

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd says the singular pronoun refers back to ما in ما تركبون.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r7.anchor: ذكر الكناية لأنه رده إلى ما في قوله: «ما تركبون» قاله أبو عبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r8.claim: Al-Farra says ظهور is plural because the singular generic noun denotes a whole class, like an army or troop.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r8.anchor: أضاف الظهور إلى واحد لأن المراد به الجنس، فصار الواحد في معنى الجمع بمنزلة الجيش والجند

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r12.claim: The command to ride on their backs refers specifically to camels: ships are boarded through their undersides, although both were named earlier; their submerged outer side may also be regarded as their interior.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r12.anchor: { لتستووا على ظهوره } يعني به الإبل خاصة بدليل ما ذكرنا، ولأن الفلك إنما تركب بطونها، ولكنه ذكرهما جميعا في أول الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r13.claim: When mounted, riders are to praise God for subduing their conveyance for use on land and sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r13.anchor: أي ركبتم عليه وذكر النعمة هو الحمد لله على تسخير ذلك لنا في البر والبحر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r14.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib's reading has من in place of الذي.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r14.anchor: وفي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب «سبحان من سخر لنا هذا»

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r15.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi interpret muqrinin as able to manage or master it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r15.anchor: أي مطيقين في قول ابن عباس والكلبي

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r16.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubayda gloss muqrinin as controlling or restraining it.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r17.claim: A further gloss is that people are not its equal in strength; someone is called another's qirn when he matches him in strength.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r17.anchor: وقيل: مماثلين في الأيد والقوة من قولهم: هو قرن فلان إذا كان مثله في القوة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r18.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r18.claim: Qutrub cites Amr ibn Ma'dikarib's poem as lexical evidence for مقرنين.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:12-13/r18.anchor: وأنشد قطرب قول عمرو بن معديكرب:

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.claim: A second, unnamed poet likewise uses مقرنينا as evidence for the word's meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r1.anchor: وقال آخر: ركبتم صعبتي أشرا وحيفا ولستم للصعاب بمقرنينا

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.claim: Muqrin can also mean a person overwhelmed by his livestock without a helper, or one who waters camels without a herder to drive them.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r2.anchor: والمقرن أيضا: الذي غلبته ضيعته يكون له إبل أو غنم ولا معين له عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit gives one derivation from the verb for being able, as if something were secured and mastered with a tether.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: وفي أصله قولان: أحدهما أنه مأخوذ من الإقران يقال: أقرن يقرن إقرانا إذا أطاق

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r4.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit's second derivation takes the word from pairing things together as they travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه مأخوذ من المقارنة وهو أن يقرن بعضها ببعض في السير

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r5.claim: God taught what riders should say on animals, and elsewhere taught Noah what to say when boarding a ship.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r5.anchor: وعرفنا في آية أخرى على لسان نوح عليه السلام ما نقول إذا ركبنا السفن وهي قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.claim: Since riding exposes people to danger, they should remember that death is certain and return to God, prepare by reforming themselves, and remain alert to a fatal accident.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r6.anchor: فلما كان الركوب مباشرة أمر محظور واتصالا بأسباب من أسباب التلف أمر ألا ينسى عند اتصاله به يومه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r7.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r7.claim: Sulayman ibn Yasar recounts travelers reciting the riding formula; one man claimed mastery over his emaciated camel, which bucked and broke his neck. Al-Mawardi transmits this account.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r7.anchor: حكى سليمان بن يسار أن قوما كانوا في سفر فكانوا إذا ركبوا قالوا: «سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين»

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi tells of a Bedouin who said he could master his mount; it ran with him and threw him, breaking his neck.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r8.anchor: وروي أن أعرابيا ركب قعودا له وقال إني لمقرن له فركضت به القعود حتى صرعته فاندقت عنقه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.claim: Uttering the formula aloud is not obligatory, but a rider should remember it when mounting, especially on a journey, and add the travel supplication asking God for company and protection from travel hardship and a bad return.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r9.anchor: وما ينبغي لعبد أن يدع قول هذا وليس بواجب ذكره باللسان فيقول متى ركب وخاصة في السفر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.claim: The supplication's phrase al-jawr ba'd al-kawr means a person's affairs becoming scattered after being in order.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r10.anchor: يعني ب «الجور بعد الكور» تشتت أمر الرجل بعد اجتماعه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r11.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r11.claim: Amr ibn Dinar recounts that Abu Ja'far rode a difficult camel and said the Prophet had taught that a devil sits on each camel's hump; riders should invoke God and tame their mounts.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14/r11.anchor: وقال عمرو بن دينار: ركبت مع أبي جعفر إلى أرض له نحو حائط يقال لها مدركة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says a devil is on each camel's hump; riders should invoke God as instructed and tame the animal for their use, since God is the one who carries them.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r1.anchor: على سنام كل بعير شيطان إذا ركبتموها فاذكروا اسم الله كما أمركم ثم امتهنوها لأنفسكم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.speaker: علي بن ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.claim: Ali ibn Rabi'a witnessed Ali ibn Abi Talib say the riding formula and a prayer for forgiveness after mounting; Ali said he had seen the Prophet do and say the same, and the Prophet marvelled that the servant knew only God forgives sins. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Ibn Khuwayzimindad transmit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن ربيعة: شهدت علي بن أبي طالب ركب دابة يوما فلما وضع رجله في الركاب قال: باسم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.claim: Al-Thalabi gives a concise version from Ali: the Prophet said bismillah when placing his foot in the stirrup and praised God on mounting, then taught a supplication on disembarking from a ship or animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r3.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي نحوه مختصرا عن علي رضي الله عنه، ولفظه عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says Satan tells someone who mounts without the formula to sing, or, if he cannot sing, to make wishes; al-Nahhas transmits this report.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r4.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: من ركب ولم يقل «سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين»

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r5.claim: The author warns against pleasure trips on horses or boats with wine and instruments, where riders drink until stupefied and remember only Satan while obeying him.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r5.anchor: ويستعيذ بالله من مقام من يقول لقرنائه: تعالوا نتنزه على الخيل أو في بعض الزوارق

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari recounts hearing of a ruler who rode from one town to another, a month's journey, while drinking; he came to himself only upon arriving home and had not noticed the trip.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r6.anchor: الزمخشري: ولقد بلغني أن بعض السلاطين ركب وهو يشرب الخمر من بلد إلى بلد بينهما مسيرة شهر

QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r7.claim: The author contrasts such heedless riders with the remembrance this verse commands.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:13-14#2/r7.anchor: فكم بين فعل أولئك الراكبين وبين ما أمر الله به في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r6.claim: Remembering the blessing means inwardly recognizing that God created the sea, winds, and ship so a person can steer it in any desired direction; they are not products of human planning, so recognition should lead to obedience and gratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r6.anchor: خلق وجه البحر ، وخلق الرياح ، وخلق جرم السفينة

RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r7.claim: Recognizing that God created sea, winds, and ship to answer human steering leads people to submit to Him and thank Him for His endless blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v27p170#2/r7.anchor: عرف أن ذلك نعمة عظيمة من الله تعالى ، فيحمله ذلك على الانقياد والطاعة له تعالى ، وعلى الاشتغال بالشكر لنعمه التي لا نهاية لها

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r1.claim: Razi lists distinct remembrances for riding a ship, riding livestock, and entering a dwelling: 11:41, 43:13, and 23:29 respectively.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى عين ذكرا معينا لركوب السفينة

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r2.claim: A riding animal greatly exceeds a human in strength and lacks reason to guide it in obeying people, yet God made its outer and inner constitution useful to them.

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r3.claim: Outwardly, the animal's four legs provide a form on which a human can sit securely.

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r4.claim: Inwardly, despite its great strength, God made the animal obedient and subject to humans; contemplating this evokes wonder at divine power and wisdom and the praise in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r4.anchor: أما خلقها الباطن ، فلأنها مع قوتها الشديدة قد خلقها الله سبحانه بحث تصير منقادة للإنسان ومسخرة له

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses muqrin as one who controls or restrains another.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : فلان مقرن لفلان ، أي ضابط له

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi derives muqrin from “making a counterpart”; calling oneself another's equal in strength means one can control or match him, and the verse says people lack the power to master ship or beast.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي : وكان اشتقاقه من قولك ضرب له قرنا

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r7.claim: People lack the strength to match or control a ship or riding animal; God alone subjects them through His knowledge, wisdom, and perfect power.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r7.anchor: فكان المعنى أنه ليس عندنا من القوة والطاقة أن نقرن هذه الدابة والفلك وأن نضبطها

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r8.claim: The report in al-Kashshaf says the Prophet said “In God's name” when putting his feet in the stirrup, then praised God and recited the subjugation remembrance after mounting.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r8.anchor: روى صاحب ( الكشفا ) : عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r9.speaker: الحسن بن علي
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r9.claim: Abu Makhlad reports that al-Hasan ibn Ali saw a man mount an animal and said, “Glory to Him who favored us with Muhammad,” praised God for making them the best community, then recited the riding remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r9.anchor: روى القاضي في ( تفسيره ) : عن أبي مخلد أن الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام : رأى رجلا ركب دابة ، فقال سبحان الذي من علينا بمحمد

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r10.speaker: رسول الله
