RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r10.claim: A report says that on a journey the Messenger said takbir three times, recited the riding remembrance, prayed for righteousness, piety, pleasing deeds, an easy journey, God's companionship, and care for his family; returning, he said they were returning repentant and praising God.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r10.anchor: وروي أيضا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنه كان إذا سافر وركب راحلته ، كبر ثلاثا

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r11.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf argues that the purpose clause shows God intended people to mount and remember Him, contradicting the Mujabbira claim that He intended unbelief and persistence in denial.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r11.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : دلت هذه الآية على خلاف قول المجبرة من وجوه الأول : أنه تعالى قال : { لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r12.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r12.claim: A second argument against the Mujabbira is that the purpose clause “so that you may settle” shows God's action is directed toward ends.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r12.anchor: الثاني : أن قوله { لتستووا } يدل على أن فعله معلل بالأغراض

RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r13.claim: A third argument says God created animals with these traits so servants would give thanks; if human acts were God's acts, this would mean He created the animals to create the phrase on a servant's tongue, though He could create the phrase without those means.
RAZI-FULL:v27p171/r13.anchor: الثالث : أنه تعالى بين أن خلق هذه الحيوانات على هذه الطبائع إنما كان لغرض أن يصدر الشكر على العبد

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.claim: The pairs refer variously to all animal species, all opposites, or male and female members of animal kinds.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r1.anchor: refers to all species of animals (IK, Q), to all opposites (R), or to the fact that all animals have both males and females (Q).

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that pairs show created things are relative and multiple, whereas their Creator is Absolute and transcends duality.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r2.anchor: According to al-Rāzī, that they are pairs indicates that they are all relative and multiple

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.claim: Seafaring and cattle are blessings; cattle serve riding and transport, warmth and clothing, food and drink, and beauty as signs of God's beneficence.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r3.anchor: mention seafaring as a blessing bestowed by God (cf. 14:32; 17:66; 22:65; 30:46) and invoke the benefits of cattle

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.claim: Muslims commonly use this supplication when traveling by land; for sea travel, they are advised to use the prayer in 11:41.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r4.anchor: The supplication given at the end of this verse is often employed by Muslims when traveling by land

STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.claim: Acknowledging that creation is made subservient to people, though they are not its equal, admits people cannot use these resources without Divine Aid.
STUDYQURAN:43:12/r5.anchor: human beings do not have the capacity to make use of these resources without Divine Aid

TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that people may ride on the backs of what they mount.
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r1.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: تذكيره يعود على ما تركبون، وما هو مذكر

TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r2.claim: A Basran grammarian says the masculine singular pronoun refers to ما تركبون, which is masculine; anʿām can be masculine or feminine, as elsewhere in the Qur’an.
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: تذكيره يعود على ما تركبون، وما هو مذكر

TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r3.claim: A Kufan grammarian explains the plural backs by the collective sense of the singular antecedent, like an army or troop.
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: أضيفت الظهور إلى الواحد، لأن ذلك الواحد في معنى جمع بمنزلة الجند والجيش

TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r4.speaker: آخر منهم
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r4.claim: Another grammarian says the phrase describes the ships: al-fulk is a collective, so its backs are plural while its pronoun is singular; collective actions can take singular or plural forms.
TAB-FULL:v20p556#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخر منهم: قيل: لتستووا على ظهره، لأنه وصف للفلك، ولكنه وحد الهاء، لأن الفلك بتأويل جمع

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r1.claim: After mounting the ships or animals Allah subjected as vehicles on land and sea, people should remember His blessing, magnify Him, and declare Him free of the partners and descriptions of the polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r1.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: ركبت دابة، فقلت: {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.claim: Abū Majliz recounts that a rider, identified by Sufyān as al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, told him to praise Allah for Islam, Muhammad, and being the best community before reciting the riding formula.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r2.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: ركبت دابة، فقلت: {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.claim: Qatāda says to say the basmala when boarding ships, the glorification formula when riding camels, and a prayer asking for a blessed landing when disembarking.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه} [الزخرف: 13] " يعلمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم في الفلك تقولون

TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.claim: Ṭāwūs would say that the ride was from Allah’s favor and grace, then recite the glorification formula.
TAB-FULL:v20p557/r4.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، أنه كان إذا ركب قال

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r1.claim: Muqrinīn means able to control or master something, from the expression for becoming a match for it and being able to handle it.

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as meaning that people were not capable.
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وما كنا له مقرنين} [الزخرف: 13] يقول: «مطيقين»

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses muqrinīn as camels, horses, mules, and donkeys.
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: {مقرنين} [إبراهيم: 49] قال: «الإبل والخيل والبغال والحمير»

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r4.claim: Qatāda says people are not capable of it, neither by their hands nor by their strength; another report summarizes this as a matter of strength.
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما كنا له مقرنين} [الزخرف: 13] «أي مطيقين، لا والله لا في الأيدي ولا في القوة»

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says people are not capable of it.
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r5.anchor: عن السدي، {وما كنا له مقرنين} [الزخرف: 13] قال: «مطيقين»

TAB-FULL:v20p560/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says people can handle these animals only through Allah; without Him they would have neither strength nor ability.
TAB-FULL:v20p560/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله جل ثناؤه: {سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين} [الزخرف: 13] قال: «لسنا له مطيقين»

SULAMI:v2p231#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r1.claim: One who recognizes God's blessings only in food, drink, and a mount has made those blessings seem small.
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : من لم يعرف نعم الله عليه إلا في مطعمه ومشربه ومركبه فقد صغر نعم الله عنده .

SULAMI:v2p231#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says ordinary people notice blessings only sometimes, missing God's gifts in every breath, blink, movement, and stillness.
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : خاطب العوام بأنهم يذكرون النعم في وقت دون وقت ولا يعرفون نعم الله عليهم في كل نفس

SULAMI:v2p231#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r3.claim: Sahl says prophets and some truthful servants were specially granted awareness of God's blessings before they vanished and of His decree concerning them.
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r3.anchor: قال سهل : خص الأنبياء وبعض الصديقين بمعرفة نعم الله عليهم قبل زوالها وحكم الله فيهم .

SULAMI:v2p231#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r4.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says riding animals should be for necessity or war in God's path, not for amusement or pride.
SULAMI:v2p231#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر في هذه الآية : ليكن ركوبكم على الدواب ضرورة عن المشي أو حربا في سبيل الله

TUSTARI:43:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:43:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:43:13/r1.claim: God gave prophets and some truthful saints awareness of His favors before they disappear and of His forbearance; anyone who recognizes blessings only in food, drink, and transport has belittled them.
TUSTARI:43:13/r1.anchor: إن الله خص الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وبعض الصديقين بمعرفة نعم الله تعالى عليهم قبل زوالها وحلم الله عنهم

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r9.claim: Istiwāʾ on the backs means settling on them, and both pronouns refer to ‘what you ride.’

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r10.claim: The blessing recalled after mounting is the utility of God’s subjection of ships and animals, such as travel and carrying loads.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r10.anchor: ذكر النعم التي ينتفع بها الإنسان بتسخيره تعالى له هذه المراكب

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r1.claim: Another possible sense is to recall God’s blessings generally, moving from mention of vehicle blessings to God Himself.
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r1.anchor: أو المراد ذكر مطلق نعمه تعالى بالانتقال من ذكر هذه النعم إليه

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r2.claim: Remembering a blessing when using it ordinarily means thanking its giver; that gratitude differs from the following glorification.
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r2.anchor: وظاهر ذكر النعمة عند استعمالها والانتفاع بها شكر منعمها

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r3.claim: The utterance glorifies God as transcendent from anything unworthy of His majesty, especially a partner in lordship or divinity; it is not itself thanks.
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r3.anchor: فإن هذا القول تسبيح وتنزيه له عما لا يليق بساحة كبريائه

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r4.claim: Reports from the Prophet and Imams about what to say when mounting vary, but include praise in addition to glorification.
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r4.anchor: ما ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في ما يقال عند الاستواء على المركوب

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r5.speaker: الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī asked a man who said the riding glorification whether he had been commanded to say it.
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r5.anchor: وروى في الكشاف عن الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام أنه رأى رجلا يركب دابة

TABATABAI:43:13-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:13-14/r6.claim: Muqrinīn means capable or able; iqrān means ability.

TABRISI:43:11-14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r10.claim: The purpose is that people ride the created conveyances; the pronoun in “their backs” refers to the word “what.”
TABRISI:43:11-14/r10.anchor: فالضمير في ظهوره يعود إلى لفظ ما

TABRISI:43:11-14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r11.claim: Riders should remember and thank God for subduing their conveyance and declare Him unlike created things.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r11.anchor: فتشكروا على تلك النعمة التي هي تسخير ذلك المركب

TABRISI:43:11-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r12.claim: God made the vehicle compliant for them, though people could not master it or match it in strength themselves.

TABRISI:43:11-14/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:43:11-14/r14.claim: Qatada says God taught people what to say when they ride.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r14.anchor: قال قتادة: قد علمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم

THALABI:v8p328/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r15.claim: The pronoun in ẓuhūrihi is singular because it refers back to the collective mā, which can denote the riding animals together.
THALABI:v8p328/r15.anchor: لتستووا على ظهوره ذكر الكناية لأنه ردها إلى ما،

THALABI:v8p329/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p329/r1.claim: Muqrinīn means able to master or control it; the sense is that people could not match its strength.
THALABI:v8p329/r1.anchor: أي مطبقين ضابطين قاهرين وهو من القرآن، كأنه أراد وما كنا مقاومين له في القوة.

THALABI:v8p329/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v8p329/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said bismillah when placing his foot in the stirrup, then on mounting praised God, recited these verses, and repeated takbīr and tahlīl three times each. No grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p329/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، إنه كان إذا وضع رجله في الركاب،

THALABI:v8p329/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p329/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p329/r4.claim: Qatada says the verse teaches what to say when riding ships or livestock and cites the prayer for a blessed landing from 23:29.
THALABI:v8p329/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: في هذه الآية يعلمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم في الفلك والأنعام تقولون:

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r1.claim: Muqrinīn means able or capable; ana muqrin laka means “I can manage you.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r1.anchor: وما كنا له مقرنين} أي مطيقين. يقال: أنا مقرن لك؛ أي مطيق لك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r2.claim: Another usage, “I am qarn to so-and-so,” means that one is his equal in strength.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r2.anchor: ويقال: هو من قولهم: أنا قرن لفلان؛ إذا كنت مثله في الشدة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r3.claim: With qarn vocalized with fatḥa, the expression means “I am his equal in age.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p395#4/r3.anchor: وإن فتحت - فقلت: أنا قرن لفلان. - أردت: أنا مثله في السن (3) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says the masculine pronoun agrees with mā, the relative pronoun “what.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: التذكير ل: ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra says “backs” is plural though it refers to a singular word with collective meaning, like army or troop.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: أضاف الظهور إلى واحد فيه معنى الجمع بمنزلة الجيش والجند

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r3.claim: The blessing to recall is God's subjection of vehicles for travel on land and sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r3.anchor: يعني النعمة بتسخير ذلك لكم، مراكب في البر والبحر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the recollection as thanking God for providing the mount and carrying the rider on it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو أن تقول: الحمد لله الذي رزقني هذا وحملني عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the recalled blessing as God's honoring people through these conveyances, supported by the statement that the children of Adam were honored and carried on land and sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس: تذكروا كرامة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r6.claim: Muqatil explains the formula as saying God made the conveyance compliant and available.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: ذلل لنا هذا المركب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r7.claim: Qatada says the ship-riding formula is taught in 11:41, while this verse teaches the formula for riding camels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: قد علمكم كيف تقولون إذا ركبتم الفلك بقوله: {بسم الله مجراها ومرساها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says people could not manage camels, ships, or the sea without God's subjection of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: ولا طاقة لنا بالإبل ولا بالفلك ولا بالبحر لولا أن الله سخره لنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r9.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r9.claim: The exegetes take muqrinīn to mean able or capable; Abu Ubayda glosses it as able to control something and cites a line about mastering difficult things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r9.anchor: ومعنى المقرن: المطيق في قول المفسرين (¬3)، قال أبو عبيدة: فلان مقرن لفلان، أي: ضابط له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r10.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r10.claim: Al-Layth derives the word from being able to handle a horse or camel; al-Zajjaj and Ibn Qutayba give similar explanations, with Ibn Qutayba likening it to an equal in strength.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r10.anchor: وقال الليث: أقرنت لهذا البرذون والبعير، أي قد أطقته، وكان اشتقاقه من قولك: صوت له قرنا مطيقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r11.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r11.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the statement looks declarative but functions as a command: if it were only a report, all people would act on it; compare 51:56, meaning God created them to be commanded to worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p16#2/r11.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: هذا كله خبر عن ظاهره، ومعناه في الباطن أمر؛ لأنه لو كان خبرا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r4.claim: Muqrinin means able to master or manage it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r4.anchor: وما كنا له مقرنين } أي: مطيقين.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.claim: A report says the Prophet said the basmala at the stirrup, praised God when mounted, recited the cited glorification and return verse, then said three takbīrs and three tahlīls.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r17.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ayağını üzengiye koyduğu zaman بِسْمِ اللهِّٰ der, hayvanın üzerine doğrulduğunda اَلْحَمْدُ لِلهِ عَلَى كُ ِّل حَالٍ.

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r18.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r18.claim: Another report says that when setting out, the Prophet took three takbīrs, recited the glorification, prayed for piety, good deeds, an eased journey and divine company, and on return praised God as a returning penitent.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r18.anchor: Yine rivayet olunmuştur ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem sefere çıkacağı vakit râhilesine bindiğinde üç tekbir alır, sonra سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا der

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.claim: A rider should see a journey as a change of state that prompts reflection on the greater journey to God, and therefore ride only for a licit purpose.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r20.anchor: bir inkılab olduğunu düşünmeli, ondan da asıl büyük yolculuğu, Allah’a olan seyr ü inkılâbı düşünmeli de o mülâhazaya göre hareket etmeli.

MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.claim: The masculine agreement in ‘what you ride so that you may settle on its backs’ follows the masculine relative pronoun mā.
MAJAZ:v2p202/r2.anchor: «والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون لتستووا على ظهوره» (12- 13) التذكير ل «ما»

MAJAZ:v2p202/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p202/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p202/r3.claim: Muqrinīn means able to control or manage something; al-Kumayt’s line says the riders cannot manage difficult mounts.
MAJAZ:v2p202/r3.anchor: «وما كنا له مقرنين» (13) ضابطين، يقال: فلان مقرن لفلان أي ضابط له مطيق، قال الكميت:

BURHAN:v4p204/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p204/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p204/r1.claim: An ‘if/when’ clause can require the commanded act before its condition, coincide with it, or follow it; Zarkashi illustrates the three timings with washing before prayer, measured recitation, and hunting or Friday prayer after their conditions.
BURHAN:v4p204/r1.anchor: وقولهم اذا فعلت كذا فيكون على ثلاثة اضرب احدها يكون المامور به قبل الفعل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r1.claim: Within one kind of compound simile, one example can gain force through more exhaustive detail than another.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r1.anchor: زيادة أحد التشبيهين مع أن جنسهما جنس واحد وتركيبهما على حقيقة واحدة بأن في أحدهما فضل استقصاء ليس في الآخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r2.claim: Saying musk is in the agate cup's bottom specifies its placement and avoids suggesting it fills the whole cup, a flaw in the less precise wording.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r2.anchor: وقوله في قرارتها مسك يبين الأمر الأول ويؤمن من دخول النقص عليه كما كان يدخل لو قال ككأس عقيق فيها مسك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r3.claim: Residual ghāliya is a more exact comparison than dry musk: moist perfume applied by fingers rises along the sides as a thin stain, like the plant's dark coloring.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r3.anchor: وأما الغالية فهي رطبة ثم هي تؤخذ بالأصابع وإذا كان كذلك فلابد في البقية منها من أن تكون قد ارتفعت عن القرارة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r4.claim: The dawn-and-crow simile maps the night's darkness onto crows and specifies pale primary feathers to evoke the light edging the dark as dawn appears.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r4.anchor: شبه ظلام الليل حين يظهر فيه الصبح بأشخاص الغربان ثم شرط أن تكون قوادم ريشها بيضا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r5.claim: The pale feather image corresponds to the fringe of darkness beside the main shaft of dawn, whose brightness makes the eye imagine white feathers.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r5.anchor: لأن تلك الفرق من الظلمة تقع في حواشيها من حيث يلي معظم الصبح وعموده لمع نور يتخيل منها في العين كشكل قوادم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r6.claim: The simile's added precision also makes dawn's forceful light seem to drive the darkness onward.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p152/r6.anchor: وتمام التدقيق والسحر في هذا التشبيه في شىء آخر وهو أن جعل ضوء الصبح لقوة ظهوره ودفعه لظلام الليل كأنه يحفز الدجى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p47/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p47/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p47/r1.claim: Calling eloquence a special arrangement of words is too general to explain it; one must specify the concrete features that distinguish correct from faulty expression and levels of excellence, as with brocade weaving.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p47/r1.anchor: فكان يكفي في معرفة نسج الديباج الكثير التصاوير أن تعلم أنه ترتيب للغزل على وجه مخصوص

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r4.claim: A poet can make the verse about subduing the mount scan by adding words until the line falls into meter.
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r4.anchor: فزاد فيه حتى انتظم له الشعر

BURHAN:v1p481/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p481/r5.speaker: النووي
BURHAN:v1p481/r5.claim: Al-Nawawi allows a ritually impure person to say Qur'anic phrases such as take the Scripture firmly or the travel supplication when intending something other than recitation.
BURHAN:v1p481/r5.anchor: قال النووي رحمه الله إذا قال

ITQAN:v2p329#5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p329#5/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p329#5/r1.claim: The word muqrinīn means able or capable.

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r11.claim: Istawā can mean to ride or board, as when people ride a conveyance or a ship.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r11.anchor: استوى أي ركب قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

DAMGHANI:v1p378/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p378/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p378/r3.claim: Moqrinin can mean owners or those able to control something.
DAMGHANI:v1p378/r3.anchor: المقرن أي المالك قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف
